citation: Jerrim, J., Austerberry, H., Crisan, C., Ingold, A., Morgan, C., Pratt, D., Smith, C., & Wiggins, M. (2015). Mathematics Mastery: Secondary Evaluation Report and Executive Summary. London: Education Endowment Foundation.
report_number: EEF project: Mathematics Mastery (Secondary). Evaluation by UCL Institute of Education, February 2015.
design: Cluster RCT (assignment = School, paired randomisation by % achieving A*-C in GCSE Eng/Maths); 50 schools randomised (25 intervention / 25 control), 7,712 pupils; analysis sample 44 schools (23 intervention, 3,251 pupils / 21 control, 2,687 pupils) = 5,938 pupils (N=5,919 in regression after covariate imputation drops); Year 7 pupils (age 11-12, grade-6/3-6 band); subject = mathematics; whole-school 'mastery' maths curriculum delivered by Ark with teacher training/PD; business-as-usual control; immediate post-test after one year of implementation (summer 2014).
problems: Effect sizes are taken directly from the report's ANCOVA/OLS regression tables, where the dependent variable (PiM score) is standardised to mean 0 / SD 1, so the 'Intervention' coefficient (Beta) is itself a standardized mean difference. The report explicitly states the section-score effect sizes are 'based upon Hedges' G' (p.34), and EEF convention treats these adjusted standardized differences as Hedges' g; the J small-sample correction is negligible at N~5,900 (df>5,000, J approximately 1.0), so g is recorded equal to Beta. impact_se is the report's school-clustered (Huber-White, STATA svy) standard error; g_var = SE^2. The headline EEF effect size in the executive summary (+0.06, 95% CI -0.04 to +0.15) is the rounded total-PiM coefficient 0.055. Models adjust for KS1 maths level, KS1 average point score, KS2 maths (linear + squared), KS2 English, FSM, ethnicity, gender, EAL. ICC for PiM test scores = 0.077 (fixed effect) / 0.069 (random effect) from Table 1 (p.14); recorded ICC = 0.077 (the design-effect-relevant between-school proportion). Calculator and non-calculator section scores are sub-components (subscale) of the total PiM and are extracted as subscale rows; the FSM-only result is a non-randomised subgroup (is_full_sample=false). n_t/n_c per row reflect the full analysis-sample split (3,251 / 2,687); exact per-section completer splits are not tabulated, only total N per regression. Note: a companion 'Mathematics Mastery: Primary Evaluation Report' (Year 1) exists; it does NOT match grade band 3-6 (Year 1 = age 5-6), so the Secondary report (Year 7) is the correct match for registry row 58 (grade 3-6).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Mathematics Mastery (single TPD/curriculum arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: GL Assessment Progress in Maths (PiM) - total score
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (summer 2014, end of one year of implementation)
effect_sizes.g_method: ANCOVA/OLS regression coefficient on the Intervention dummy; dependent variable = total PiM raw score standardised to mean 0, SD 1, so Beta is a standardized mean difference (= adjusted mean diff / SD). Recorded directly as g (J correction negligible at N=5,919). SE = report's school-clustered (Huber-White, STATA svy) SE; g_var = SE^2.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.33 Table 9 (All children, Intervention row); also p.6 Table (exec summary, +0.06 / -0.04 to +0.15)
effect_sizes.notes: Headline/confirmatory outcome. Maths -> STEM per spec. Total PiM score across calculator + non-calculator sections (raw max 50 marks). Not statistically significant (p>0.05). N=5,919 in regression (19 obs dropped for missing covariates); analysis sample 5,938 pupils. PiM is a commercially published, independently developed standardized maths test (GL Assessment). Around 40% of PiM questions cover content outside the Year 7 MM curriculum.
